chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Second Texas tour: colored dances and the Dallas union
summary: On a later Texas tour they play mostly colored dances, the Dallas union tries to keep them out, and Driggs raises other Texas bands.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: But that's the second time around. You had already come back--you'd been up north, you'd come back to Texas. You went through Texas a second time around; this is in the early thirties now when you went back to Texas. You went back to Texas during the depres-
sion, before the band broke up, you went back to Texas at one time; I'm pretty sure. Everything had changed by that time.
We went back to Texas-- I'm trying to think what year that was--I guess we had made a tour of Texas but we were playing mostly colored dances. Yeah, we were playing mostly colored dances.
You couldn't get in the white hotels?

Well the unions--in fact, the unions in Dallas tried to keep us out of (inaudible), because the band that they had in there--I'm trying to think of the name, I'll know it when I hear it--they were from Texas, a Dallas band. I can't think of the guy.
No, it wasn't Jimmy George; we met him later.
Is he the guy that plays the two clarinets?
There was another guy, Hogan Handcock (phonetic spelling) from Texas, a trombone player.
That's one of the ones that Harry James had in the group.
You didn't play down in Mineral Wells did you?
